# Dress rehearsal on 2025-26 — the locked pipeline, end to end, on realised outcomes

**Generated by `scripts/render_rehearsal_note.py` from the evaluator payloads; every number is read from an artifact. Study A of `prelock-program-preregistration-2026-09-04.md` (ATI-2961). Prediction set built 2026-09-04 (status `draft`) from `import_signings_2025_both_competitions_2026-09-04.json`; interval `conformal` (nominal 95%, split conformal half-width 7.78 PIR/36 calibrated on walk-forward folds 2020–2024 (547 out-of-sample rows); Study C, Amendment 8); outcomes from `build_realised_outcomes.py` season 2025.**

## Specification

| Choice | This study | Alternative considered |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | one 2025-26 import (signing), as the lock's unit | pair-level rows (rejected — no pair-level study runs the refusals, the censoring or the interval) |
| **Pipeline** | the committed collector → builder (fitted on seasons ≤ 2024, Amendment 8 interval calibrated through 2024) → evaluator, unchanged except for the population filter Amendment 8 Change 4 names | a re-fit that sees 2025 (rejected — the rehearsal must be out of sample as the lock will be) |
| **Primary population** | imports whose full-season first RS round is ≤ 3; the full predicted set as sensitivity | the full roster as primary (rejected — an end-of-season roster carries midseason arrivals the lock's preseason collection never sees) |
| **Reads** | the evaluator's own: P1, P2, S1, S2, R8 censoring at ≥ 5 / ≥ 8 / ≥ 15 games, MAE by source-season lag, verdict, at two as-of dates | — |
| **What it may change** | a pipeline defect (crash, join, censor count) is fixed and recorded; a number is reported; no 2026-27 rule moves (§8) | — |

## The prediction set

* Predicted 88, refused 428 (R1 94, R2 176, R3 10, R5 100, R9 48); combined arm 73, per-league only 15.
* Outcomes: 647 players in the 2025-26 box scores, 533 with ≥ 8 games, 494 first seen by RS round 3.
* K_LAG 0.9363 from cohorts strictly before 2025; interval: nominal 95%, split conformal half-width 7.78 PIR/36 calibrated on walk-forward folds 2020–2024 (547 out-of-sample rows); Study C, Amendment 8 (source `interval_params_rehearsal_through_2024.json`).

At 2026-01-31 on every predicted player (59 scored, 29 censored) the verdict is **FAIL**: the model's MAE is +5.9% relative to B0 against the 12.8% margin (not met), the paired CI covers zero (Δ +0.2511 [-0.5996, +1.0629]), so P1 fails; the model does not beat the oracle constant B1b, does not beat RTM, and the interval covers 0.881 (outside the band). At 2026-01-31 on full-season first_round <= 3 (56 scored, 10 censored) the verdict is **FAIL**: the model's MAE is +3.6% relative to B0 against the 12.8% margin (not met), the paired CI covers zero (Δ +0.1476 [-0.7128, +0.9515]), so P1 fails; the model does not beat the oracle constant B1b, does not beat RTM, and the interval covers 0.893 (outside the band). At 2026-06-30 on every predicted player (68 scored, 20 censored) the verdict is **FAIL**: the model's MAE is +9.9% relative to B0 against the 12.8% margin (not met), the paired CI covers zero (Δ +0.3839 [-0.4790, +1.2145]), so P1 fails; the model does not beat the oracle constant B1b, does not beat RTM, and the interval covers 0.941 (inside the band). At 2026-06-30 on full-season first_round <= 3 (58 scored, 8 censored) the verdict is **FAIL**: the model's MAE is +10.2% relative to B0 against the 12.8% margin (not met), the paired CI covers zero (Δ +0.3921 [-0.5388, +1.2385]), so P1 fails; the model does not beat the oracle constant B1b, does not beat RTM, and the interval covers 0.931 (inside the band). P1 power was read before the evaluator ran: 0.801 at n=88, 0.68 at n=66 (`power_rehearsal_2025.json`). SE of the Δ-vs-B0 contrast at the scored n, paired bootstrap against the walk-forward's pooled SE scaled by √(n_pooled/n) — 2026-01-31 every predicted player: realised 0.42 against 0.35 scaled (×1.22); 2026-01-31 full-season first_round <= 3: realised 0.42 against 0.36 scaled (×1.19); 2026-06-30 every predicted player: realised 0.43 against 0.32 scaled (×1.33); 2026-06-30 full-season first_round <= 3: realised 0.45 against 0.35 scaled (×1.29). The power line is for the CI clause alone (its method: `se_pooled = CI width / (2*1.96); se_n = se_pooled * sqrt(n_p…`); P1's 12.8% margin clause has no power statement there. Which clause binds at each read, from the read's own numbers — 2026-01-31 every predicted player: 1.96·SE = 0.831 vs margin·MAE_B0 = 0.546, the CI clause binds; 2026-01-31 full-season first_round <= 3: 1.96·SE = 0.832 vs margin·MAE_B0 = 0.518, the CI clause binds; 2026-06-30 every predicted player: 1.96·SE = 0.847 vs margin·MAE_B0 = 0.494, the CI clause binds; 2026-06-30 full-season first_round <= 3: 1.96·SE = 0.889 vs margin·MAE_B0 = 0.490, the CI clause binds. Where the CI clause binds, the missing clause changes no power figure; the realised SE does (Amendment 9). Under §8 of the program pre-registration none of this moves a 2026-27 rule; a PARTIAL is read as the base document reads one.

## The walk-forward's own fold for the same season (T-A2)

| source | n | MAE model | MAE B0 | relative to B0 | Δ vs one global scalar [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| walk-forward fold 2025 (`walkforward_per_season.csv`) | 127 | 3.312 | 3.732 | +11.2% | +0.1562 [-0.0025, +0.3142] |

Reading, from the two tables: the rehearsal's improvement over B0 runs +3.6% to +10.2% across its reads; the walk-forward's 2025 fold, at pair level on 127 rows, gave +11.2%, which itself does not meet the 12.8% margin. The pipeline reproduces the fold; the season, not the pipeline, is under the margin.

Study D's prediction interval for a new season's Δ vs B0 is [-0.086, +1.712] (pooled +0.813, k = 6). 4 of 4 rehearsal reads fall inside it (2026-01-31 every predicted player (+0.251), 2026-01-31 full-season first_round <= 3 (+0.148), 2026-06-30 every predicted player (+0.384), 2026-06-30 full-season first_round <= 3 (+0.392)). A season like 2025-26 was inside the forecast before the rehearsal ran; the rehearsal found one.

The fold scores pair-level newcomer rows (every player with ≥ 8 games on both sides), the rehearsal scores signings through the refusals and the censor; a rehearsal that lands near the fold is the pipeline reproducing the walk-forward on the season the walk-forward already had, not new evidence about the factors.

## Threats, as pre-registered, and what happened

* T-A1 end-of-season roster: handled by the primary-population filter; the midseason share is the gap between the two population rows above.
* T-A2 the 2025 fold is the walk-forward's last window at pair level: this note is evidence about the *pipeline*, not new evidence about the factors.
* T-A3 name join: unmatched imports are refused with a code and counted above, never dropped.
* T-A4 EuroCup 2025-26 destination completeness is asserted by the Amendment 5 table, not assumed here.
* T-A5 (found by the rehearsal, not pre-registered) mid-season coverage: the conformal half-width is calibrated on full-season rows; at a mid-season checkpoint the scored players have fewer games, their per-36 outcome is noisier, and a fixed half-width under-covers. Study C rejected the games-scaled family on full-season data. Prediction, not a fix: the 2026-27 mid-season S2 read will likely fall under the band the same way, and the season-end read is the one that counts.

## What this licenses

That the lock-day sequence of Amendment 7 runs end to end on real outcomes and returns the pre-registered reads, with the censoring and the population filter behaving as written. It licenses nothing about 2026-27.
